page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core of an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, and the processor includes a 50 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It also includes 66 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned at the lower end of the compute spectrum. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor performance in the bottom 10% to 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds registering at 9.64 GB/sec and 6.5 GB/sec respectively. This hardware profile exhibits lower performance in compute-intensive tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4-2s_v3 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require a large memory footprint but have low CPU demands. The inclusion of local SSD storage and Premium Storage capability allows for reliable disk operations. This server is best suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as small database caching, lightweight Redis deployments, or basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
